summary: Executed backend + frontend regression on expenses scope/category changes using public preview URL. Requested expense features passed end-to-end; auth playbook checks still show known hardening gaps.

minor.issue: No brute-force lockout after 5 failed logins (valid login still succeeds immediately after failures).
access-control-allow-origin is '*' (not explicit allowlist for credentialed auth posture).
No app-issued HttpOnly auth session cookie observed; auth remains token-in-body flow.

action_items: Implement brute-force lockout/rate-limit on /api/auth/login after repeated failed attempts.
Replace wildcard CORS with explicit origin allowlist aligned with credentialed auth policy.
If cookie-based auth is required by security policy, implement app-issued HttpOnly cookie flow.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/server.py is still a large monolith (~1600+ LOC), increasing regression risk and reducing testability.
Password hashing implementation uses bcrypt.hashpw(...), compatible with expected $2b$ bcrypt format.
ensure_default_admin() returns early when admin exists, so changed ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD does not update existing admin record (seed_admin non-idempotent vs requested behavior).
seed_data_creation: Created temporary TEST ITER18 expense records through API/UI flows and cleaned them with /app/backend/tests/test_iteration18_cleanup_test_records.py.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Requested expense scope/category behavior is passing in both API and UI (including separate voucher panels by year and death-benefit-only fields). Remaining open items are auth hardening deviations (lockout, wildcard CORS, no HttpOnly app auth cookie).
rca of the issue: Auth RCA: login handler performs direct credential verification but has no failed-attempt counter/lockout branch; CORS middleware currently responds with wildcard allow-origin; auth response returns JWT in JSON body without setting an application session cookie. Repro: run iter18 auth checks + inspect OPTIONS headers file.
